assessment.prompt: In a simple circuit, a battery is connected to a bulb by wires and the bulb lights up. If you cut one wire, why does the bulb go out?
assessment.expected_answer: The circuit is broken, so charge cannot flow in a complete loop.
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: Opening a branch removes its current path; source and branch meters recompute.

assessment.prompt: You rub a balloon on your hair and it sticks to a wall. This is an example of static electricity because...
assessment.expected_answer: rubbing charges the balloon, which then attracts the neutral wall.
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: No static-charge transfer, dielectric polarization or balloon–wall attraction.

assessment.prompt: Three 1.5 V cells are joined end to end in a row to make one battery. What is the total voltage, in volts?
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: Three 1.5 V cells produce 4.5 V; each cell orientation is explicit.

assessment.prompt: A 6 V battery lights two identical bulbs joined one after the other in a single loop. The two bulbs share the voltage equally. How many volts are across one bulb?
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: Two equal 6 Ω loads in a 6 V series loop each show 3 V; the third schematic edge is explicitly an ideal short.

assessment.prompt: Two bulbs are wired with one battery in a single loop. When one bulb is unscrewed, both go dark. How are they wired?
assessment.expected_answer: In series: the charge must pass through both bulbs in turn.
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: Opening either of two series loads gives zero current; this is an ideal ohmic-load analogue.

assessment.prompt: Household wires have a copper core inside a plastic sleeve. Why those two materials?
assessment.expected_answer: Copper conducts the current; plastic insulates the hand.
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: Finite resistors, ideal wires and open branches are distinct, but copper/plastic material microphysics is absent.

assessment.prompt: Two 1.5 V cells and one 3 V cell are joined end to end in a single row. What is the total voltage, in volts?
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: Editable 1.5 V,1.5 V,3 V cells give a 6 V total; signed cancellation is exact for entered canonical decimals.

assessment.prompt: A battery lights two identical bulbs on separate parallel loops. Each bulb draws 0.4 A. What total current, in amperes, leaves the battery?
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: Two 15 Ω parallel branches at 6 V carry 0.4 A each; source supplies 0.8 A.

assessment.prompt: A string of fairy lights keeps glowing when one bulb fails. How must the bulbs be wired?
assessment.expected_answer: In parallel, so each bulb sits on its own loop to the battery.
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: Opening a parallel branch preserves the other branch voltages/current for an ideal source.

assessment.prompt: You pull off a wool jumper in a dark room and hear tiny crackles and see small sparks. Explain what is happening.
assessment.expected_answer: Rubbing transfers electrons between the wool and your other clothes, leaving them oppositely charged. When the built-up static charge grows large enough it jumps across the small air gap as a spark.
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: No electrostatic discharge or ionization/breakdown model.

assessment.prompt: You push a bar magnet quickly into a coil of wire connected to a meter, and the meter deflects. If you hold the magnet still inside the coil, what does the meter read?
assessment.expected_answer: Zero, because current is induced only while the flux changes.
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: Actual changing external flux and a held constant field are compared; no moving finite bar-magnet field/coil geometry is solved.

assessment.prompt: Two long parallel wires carry current in the same direction. What happens between them?
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: No parallel-current wire force model.

assessment.prompt: A resistor of 4 ohms has a voltage of 12 volts across it. Using Ohm's law, what current in amperes flows through it?
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: 12 V/4 Ω gives 3 A and 36 W in the single-load preset.

assessment.prompt: A 12 V supply drives a current of 0.50 A through a small heater. What power, in watts, does the heater dissipate?
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: 12 V across 24 Ω gives 0.5 A and 6 W.

assessment.prompt: A strong magnet dropped down a vertical copper pipe takes several seconds to emerge, while through an identical plastic pipe it falls in a fraction of a second. Why?
assessment.expected_answer: Induced currents in the copper oppose the magnet’s motion.
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: Lenz torque and motor/field/heat/storage power are calculated for a uniform-field coil; no copper-pipe eddy-current field or falling-magnet trajectory.

assessment.prompt: A 3 ohm and a 6 ohm resistor are connected in parallel across a battery. How does the combined resistance compare with the 3 ohm resistor on its own?
assessment.expected_answer: It is 2 ohms, below either resistor on its own.
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: 3 Ω in parallel with 6 Ω gives a 2 Ω equivalent resistance.

assessment.prompt: A 240 V supply drives a current of 2.0 A through a heater. What is the heater's resistance, in ohms?
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: 240 V,120 Ω gives 2 A.

assessment.prompt: A 5 ohm resistor and a 7 ohm resistor are connected in series. What is the total resistance, in ohms?
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: 5 Ω+7 Ω gives a 12 Ω series equivalent resistance.

assessment.prompt: A transformer with more turns on its secondary coil than on its primary is fed with alternating current. What happens at the output?
assessment.expected_answer: The voltage is stepped up and the current stepped down.
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: No two-winding transformer, coupled inductance, secondary loading or port-power model.

assessment.prompt: A bicycle dynamo lights its lamp only while the wheel is turning. Why?
assessment.expected_answer: A voltage appears only while the flux through the coil changes.
assessment.representation_or_remaining_scope: A prescribed rotating coil produces emf/current with magnetic torque and required motor power; no rotation in a steady field gives no generated emf. Bicycle mechanism remains an analogue.
